alignments.note: Emphatic subject pronoun; the verb's own person is carried by the auxiliary *didst* inside the verb's unit under rule 9.
Anarthrous vocative. The ASV supplies no address word, so nothing under rule 89's anarthrous clause attaches and the noun stands on its own word. Reordered to second position, which rule 15 permits.
`κατ᾿ ἀρχάς` is spread over separate English words, so rule 94's precondition for a compound unit fails and rule 2 splits the pair: the preposition takes its own *in*.
The Greek is anarthrous, so under rule 51's anarthrous clause the supplied *the* is a rule 7 helper on the noun it determines, headed on the noun.

`θεμελιόω` is rendered by the support phrase *didst lay the foundation*, whose supplied determiner and auxiliary ride inside the unit under rules 7 and 9. Rule 17's support/light-verb clause heads it on the meaning-bearing complement *foundation*, as *make straight* heads on *straight*. Rule 91's operational test confirms this: the lemma's other corpus units spend *grounded* (EPH.3.17) and *establish* (1PE.5.10), neither of which stands here, so rule 104 sends the query to the root family, where `θεμέλιος` is *foundation* throughout — *foundation* is what carries the lexeme and *lay* is the light verb. A head on *lay* is the competing reading and would be defensible only if *lay* were read as glossing the lexeme.

Rule 21's shape: the article takes the English determiner and the *of* in front of it rides with it, headed on *the* under rule 17. Note that the *of* does not realize this article's case — `τὴν γῆν` is an accusative object and English marks no accusative with *of*; it is licensed by the support frame *lay the foundation of*. The competing reading is therefore to put *of* inside that frame's unit (*didst lay the foundation of*) and leave the article a bare *the*, as rule 91's TIT.3.2 `βλασφημεῖν` → *to speak evil of* does. I took the article reading because rule 67's article-carrier clause hands a determiner-bearing article the whole frame including its trailing *of* even where the case is accusative and does not license it — `τὴν χάριν` → *in regard of this* — and because TIT.3.2 had no determiner-bearing article competing for the word.
Head noun, left bare because the preceding article took the determiner and the *of* under rule 21.
Coordinating conjunction opening the second clause.
Rule 19: the article surfaces as *the*. The ASV moves the whole subject phrase in front of the copula, which rule 15 permits.
Expressed copula, so nothing is supplied and rules 53, 63 and 68 do not arise.

Predicate nominal, fronted in the Greek and inverted by the ASV. `ἔργα` is anarthrous — the following `τῶν` is genitive plural and governs `χειρῶν`, not this noun — so the supplied *the* is a rule 7 helper on it under rule 51's anarthrous clause.

Rule 20: the genitive `σου` is present and free — rule 76's availability test is satisfied, the pronoun carrying no other English word — so it takes the possessive *thy*, the article governing `χειρῶν` realizes nothing, and the case preposition *of* stays with the noun.
Discontinuous under rule 15, the possessive standing between: rule 20 leaves *of* with the noun where the possessive displaces the article.
Rule 20: the genitive pronoun takes the possessive.

review_notes: Every unit's source and target membership, status and head is unchanged from the accepted alignment; the correction is confined to notes. The partition was already complete and correct — all 16 source ids and all 22 target ids appear exactly once.

The `τήν` unit's note previously described *of* as a case preposition. It is not: `τὴν γῆν` is the accusative object of `ἐθεμελίωσας`, and English marks no accusative with *of*. The *of* is licensed by the support frame *lay the foundation of*, which makes its placement a materially contested edge that rule 16 requires the note to name. The competing reading puts *of* inside the verb's unit (*didst lay the foundation of*) and leaves `τήν` a bare *the*, on the model of rule 91's TIT.3.2 `βλασφημεῖν` → *to speak evil of*. The article reading was kept because rule 67's article-carrier clause hands a determiner-bearing article a supplied frame's trailing *of* even where the case does not license it (`τὴν χάριν` → *in regard of this*, also accusative), and because TIT.3.2 had no determiner-bearing article competing for that word.

The head of `ἐθεμελίωσας` is the other contested point and the note now settles it by rule 91's operational test rather than by rule 17 alone: the lemma's corpus units spend *grounded* (EPH.3.17) and *establish* (1PE.5.10), neither of which appears here, so rule 104 sends the query to the root family, where `θεμέλιος` is *foundation*. That is positive evidence for *foundation* over *lay*, which the accepted note lacked.

The two articles of this verse are decided differently, and deliberately: `τήν` before `γῆν` takes the determiner under rule 21, while `τῶν` before `χειρῶν` is `unrepresented` under rule 20 because `σου` is free — rule 76's availability test — to take *thy*. A reference comparison will report the empty `τῶν` as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.

`κατ᾿ ἀρχάς` is split rather than compounded because rule 94's precondition is a single English word and the ASV wrote three; `οἱ οὐρανοί` and `ἔργα` are crossed relative to the Greek order by the ASV's inversion of a fronted predicate nominal, which rule 15 permits, and no intervening word is absorbed. The vocative's move to second position is the same permission.
